newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grains - Japan to finish buying 3Q corn needs.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grains - Japan to finish buying 3Q corn needs.

text.p: Japan will finish buying all of its U.S. corn requirements for July-September shipment by next week before U.S. cash prices and freight rates rise further, traders said on Monday.
"We're recommending local feed makers to buy U.S. corn sooner, given the firming U.S. cash prices and freight rates," a corn trader at a major trade house said.
Japanese corn premiums firmed to about 90 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT May futures, against 89-90 cents last week.
Freight rates for nearby shipments on the U.S. Gulf/Japan route for Panamax-sized vessels were quoted at US$21.50 a tonne, against around $21.25 last week, traders said.

Japanese buyers said they were not willing to buy Chinese corn at this stage, as its offer prices still exceeded those of U.S. origins. Chinese corn prices were seen averaging around $135 a tonne FOB Dalian over the last three months, they said.
South Africa, which gives corn export offers to Japan at this time of the year, is more quiet than usual, traders said.
In South Korea, corn buyers are expected to stay away from the market this week after having covered their needs up to September 1997, traders said.
"Most of the buyers are well-covered (up to) September arrival," said one trader in Korea. "They'll probably stay sidelined for an additional two months or so."
Dealers said the price of corn was likely to bounce back this week. "The price has hit the bottom, and it's about time we saw a rebound," the trader said.
The Korean corn market will also be watching out for a report from a U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) report due out later on Monday, traders said.
Korean buyers of hard red winter wheat are likely to also remain on the sidelines this week, they added.
